author: NorthEast News Desk
body: West Lebanon’s Route 12A dry bridge is scheduled to close at 7 a.m. Monday, September 14, beginning a yearlong demolition and replacement project on one of the city’s busiest local connections. The 77-year-old span links South Main Street with the Route 12A shopping district and carries about 10,000 vehicles on a typical day.

The city’s posted detour will send Plainfield-bound traffic up Seminary Hill to Interstate 89 north and Exit 20. Drivers traveling the opposite direction are directed to I-89 south, Exit 19 and Miracle Mile. Officials are urging motorists to use the signed route instead of smaller local roads, which became congested during an emergency closure in March 2025.

Pedestrians and bicyclists will retain access through a temporary footbridge next to the construction site, although cyclists are encouraged to dismount while crossing. The closure gives contractors room to remove the deteriorated 145-foot bridge and start building its replacement. Because the span also serves buses, emergency vehicles, workers and shoppers, the advance notice and temporary crossing are intended to reduce the disruption that accompanied last year’s sudden shutdown.
dek: The 77-year-old Route 12A span closes Monday for demolition and replacement, redirecting roughly 10,000 daily vehicles to Interstate 89.
headline: West Lebanon dry bridge closes Monday for yearlong replacement
